name: Chef John's Bacon and Asparagus Dutch Baby
headnote: Chef John (John Mitzewich) gives just a couple of lines: he had been noticing savoury, non-breakfast Dutch babies on restaurant menus and wanted to make one with bacon and asparagus. His only technical steer is that a 12-inch cast iron skillet is the right pan, with a cook's note that the recipe feeds two generously or four modestly. The method itself carries the rest, rendering the bacon and briefly cooking the asparagus in the skillet before the batter goes in and the pan hits a 475F oven.
comment_digest: The highest-voted review (12 helpful, Redcaddy97) says to follow it exactly, that 1 cup of asparagus really is enough provided it is sliced thinly, and that broccoli, sausage or diced ham would all substitute; leftovers were good cold the next day. Mushrooms are another reported addition, and a non-cast-iron high-heat skillet worked for one reviewer. Salt is the quantity most often adjusted down: one reduced it to half a teaspoon and would omit it entirely when using bacon, noting the bacon fat is not drained but the result still was not greasy. A couple of reviewers report that it does not puff much and eats like a frittata or thin-crust pizza; one suggests slightly less flour. Whole wheat flour was tried once and blamed for a dull texture. Smoked paprika substitutes for the cayenne if you want no heat.
flags: Headnote is only two sentences on the page; comment volume is small (31 reviews) and only one review carries a helpfulness count.
